summary:
Every rating in the model is running identical splits right now, which is the headline: R1 through R4 are all 4-1 (80%, n=5) across trends, runs, sp, bullpen, and hitting over the last 14 days, while bullpen_fatigue is ice cold at 0-5 across the board with a 5-loss streak on every single rating. That's not noise — it's a clean signal to fade bullpen_fatigue-driven picks entirely today and lean into sp, which carries a 3-game win streak on every rating tier on top of its hot 14-day number. The strong-play ledger backs this up: R2 strong plays are +2.0u over the last 14 days (75%, n=4) and +4.0u over 30 days (73%, n=11), the best returning unit of the four ratings right now, with R3 close behind at +1.0u/14d but a stronger season anchor (58%, +92.0u, n=462). R4 strong plays have cooled to -1.0u over 30 days despite a hot 14-day window, so treat R4 strong plays as live but not hot.

On today's board, prioritize any game where trends+sp or trends+runs both land on the same side — those combos are hitting 58.0% (370-268, n=638) and 57.3% (404-301, n=705) for the season and align with the current sp hot streak, giving you the best double-confirmation signal available. If MIL, TBR, BOS, or LAD show up as the model's pick today, lean in hard: LAD strong plays are 28-7 (80%, +27.0u) and BOS strong plays are 22-7 (76%, +19.0u), both well clear of the pack. Avoid NYY regardless of rating agreement — strong plays on NYY are 9-14 (39%, -4.0u), the only team on the leaderboard bleeding units when the model likes them. With all four ratings moving in lockstep today, the differentiator is category, not rating: trust sp-driven picks, discount bullpen_fatigue-driven ones, and let team trends on LAD/BOS/TBR/MIL break any ties.
